bindings.label: A man in his 40s has a 3-month history of dark red circular lesions in his right axilla with severe pruritus.
Patient is a man in his 40s with a 3-month history of discrete, dark red, circular lesions in the right axilla and severe pruritus that wakes him at night.

Physical examination revealed 3 well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion limited to the right axilla; no other lesions were noted on skin or mucous membranes; Wood lamp examination was negative.
Patient denied recent trauma, similar lesions, pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms (e.g., fever, chills); medical history was unremarkable; he noted no environmental triggers or new medications.
Treatment with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, and discontinuation of underarm deodorant yielded no improvement.
Skin biopsy shows lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction, consistent with interface dermatitis such as lichen planus or lupus erythematosus
Autoimmune serology tests were not obtained (no ANA/anti-Ro/anti-La results available)
Pathologist analysis concludes the clinical and histopathologic features are highly consistent with lichen planus
Pathologist analysis states negative Wood lamp, absent scale, and failed antifungal treatment exclude superficial fungal infection and allergic contact dermatitis
Pathologist analysis notes DIF and autoimmune serology were not obtained, so cutaneous lupus remains a secondary differential
